questions.question: A linear program has a variable $x_j$ that is unrestricted in sign. Which substitution makes all variables nonnegative while keeping every possible value of $x_j$?
options: $x_j=x_j^+\cdot x_j^-$ with $x_j^+,x_j^-\ge0$
$x_j=x_j^++x_j^-$ with $x_j^+,x_j^-\ge0$
$x_j=-x_j^-$ with $x_j^-\ge0$
$x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-$ with $x_j^+,x_j^-\ge0$

questions.question: Why is an unrestricted variable $x_j$ replaced by $x_j^+-x_j^-$ before the simplex method is applied?
options: Because simplex works only with variables that are nonnegative.
Because negative values are meaningless in every linear program.
Because simplex cannot handle negative objective coefficients.
Because the substitution makes the optimal solution unique.

questions.question: In a linear program with an unrestricted variable $x_2$, a modeller replaces $x_2$ by $x_2^+-x_2^-$ in every constraint but keeps $x_2$ in the objective. What is wrong?
options: Nothing, since the objective does not restrict the variables.
The constraints should keep $x_2$ and only the objective changes.
The objective's $x_2$ is now a separate variable; replace it too.
The objective should use $x_2^+$ only, since it is nonnegative.

questions.question: A model requires $x_1\le0$ for a variable describing a reduction in stock. How is $x_1$ replaced by a nonnegative variable?
After solving the transformed model, a solver reports values for $x_j^+$ and $x_j^-$. How is the original decision $x_j$ obtained?
options: $x_j=x_j^+$, since $x_j^-$ is an auxiliary variable only
$x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-$, the difference of the parts
$x_j=\max\{x_j^+,x_j^-\}$, the larger part
$x_j=x_j^++x_j^-$, the total of both parts

questions.question: In the constraint $2x_1+3x_2\le6$, $x_1\ge0$ and $x_2$ is unrestricted. Which constraint results after the substitution $x_2=x_2^+-x_2^-$?
An unrestricted variable is written as $x=x^+-x^-$ with $x^+,x^-\ge0$. Which pair $(x^+,x^-)$ does not represent the value $x=-2$?
After substituting $x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-$, must the condition $x_j^+\cdot x_j^-=0$ (at most one part positive) be added to the model?
options: Yes, otherwise the original value of $x_j$ cannot be recovered.
No: objective and constraints depend only on $x_j^+-x_j^-$.
Yes, otherwise the transformed model would have no optimum.
No, since $x_j^+$ and $x_j^-$ can never both be positive.

questions.question: Both parts in $x=x^+-x^-$ are nonnegative. Why can $x$ still take every real value?
options: Because $x$ is recovered as the larger of $x^+$ and $x^-$.
Because only $x^+\ge0$ is required, while $x^-$ is free.
Because $x^+=x$, $x^-=0$ for $x\ge0$ and $x^+=0$, $x^-=-x$ otherwise.
Because $x$ can only take the values $x^+$ or $-x^-$, which cover both.

questions.question: For $\max\,3x_1-2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\le4$, $x_1-x_2\le6$, $x_1\ge0$, $x_2$ unrestricted in sign, a solver for the transformed model returns $(x_1,x_2^+,x_2^-)=(5,2,3)$. What does this solution mean for the original model?
options: It is invalid, since both parts of $x_2$ are positive.
It gives the same decision $(5,-1)$ and value 17.
It is feasible but has a lower value than $(5,0,1)$.
It gives $x_2=5$, the sum of both parts.

questions.question: A model has $x_1\ge0$, $x_2$ unrestricted, $x_3\le0$ and $x_4$ unrestricted. After the transformations, how many nonnegative variables does it have?
options: 4 variables
7 variables
6 variables
8 variables

questions.question: How do the feasible solutions of an LP with unrestricted $x_j$ correspond to those of the model with $x_j=x_j^+-x_j^-$, $x_j^+,x_j^-\ge0$?
options: Each transformed solution gives one original; each original has many.
Each transformed solution has many originals, sharing $x_j^+$.
The models have no common solutions, since their variables differ.
One to one: each original solution has exactly one transformed version.

questions.question: For $\max\,3x_1-2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\le4$, $x_1-x_2\le6$, $x_1\ge0$, $x_2$ unrestricted in sign, the transformed feasible region contains $(5,t,1+t)$ for every $t\ge0$, so it is unbounded. Does this make the transformed objective unbounded?
options: Yes, since an unbounded region always gives an unbounded objective.
No, since the transformation forbids $t>0$ in the first place.
Yes, since $x_2^-$ can grow and has a positive coefficient.
No, since along this direction the objective value stays at 17.

questions.question: For $\max\,3x_1-2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\le4$, $x_1-x_2\le6$, $x_1\ge0$, $x_2$ unrestricted in sign, a modeller substitutes $x_2=x_2^+-x_2^-$ in both constraints but writes the objective as $\max\,3x_1-2x_2^+$, omitting $x_2^-$. The flawed model reports the optimal point $(5,0,1)$. Which value does it report, and is it correct?
options: 17, and it is correct, as the point is optimal
15, but the true value of $(5,-1)$ is 17
15, and it is correct, as the constraints are right
13, but the true value of $(5,-1)$ is 17

questions.question: A cost model is $\min\,x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1\ge-6$, $x_2-x_1\ge2$, $x_1\le0$ (a stock reduction) and $x_2\ge0$. A student substitutes $x_1=x_1^-$ with $x_1^-\ge0$, forgetting the minus sign. What happens?
options: The optimum $-6$ at $(-6,0)$ is found anyway.
The model becomes unbounded below.
It reports cost 4 at $(0,2)$ instead of $-6$.
It reports cost $-6$ but at $(0,2)$.

questions.question: A model has $x_1\le0$ and $x_2\ge0$, and contains $3x_1+x_2\ge-6$. With $x_1=-x_1^-$, $x_1^-\ge0$, which constraint results?
